notes: Paper (An, Pospelov, Pradler, Ritz 2020, arXiv:2006.13929) sets NEW 90% C.L. limits on solar-emitted dark photons (kinetic mixing epsilon vs mA') using XENON1T S2-only data, superseding XENON10 bounds by a factor of a few. This is a solar-flux (non-DM) bound, so no local DM density assumed. The pre-analysis hint of AxionElectron is incorrect; the constrained coupling is the dark photon kinetic mixing. No numerical table is provided: data_points are approximate values read off Fig. 1 (left panel, red 'XENON1T (S2)' line, Stueckelberg hard-mass case), following the known epsilon ~ 1/m scaling at low mass with a minimum of a few x 1e-15 around 10-100 eV; treat as approximate digitization. The paper also fits the XENON1T excess with dark photon DM (best fit mA'=2.8 keV, eps=8.4e-16, rho_dm=0.3 GeV/cm^3), but that is a favored region, not an exclusion limit, and is not included in data_points.
